title: RESEARCH CAPACITY BUILDING IN AYURVEDA
body_text:
PRAYATNA is a flagship initiative of the Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS) to foster scientific writing skills among Ayurveda PG/Ph.D Scholars. The scheme is aimed at improving the quality of publications in the Ayurveda sector for effective dissemination and high-impact publications.
In this scheme, the colleges / Institutes apply through the expression of interest (EoI) followed by the two online orientation sessions focusing on the basics of scientific writing, followed by individual manuscript assistance to the Scholars. After the review, a physical workshop of 3 days is conducted at the Institutes to provide hands-on support to the Scholars and culminating in publication-ready manuscripts.
CCRAS Digital Initiatives Dashboard has been developed by Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS) as an integrated platform for showcasing the Council's web-based and digital resources to improve their accessibility and for facilitating dissemination of research outputs and institutional resources on a single web-based platform. The dashboard is available at dashboard.ccras.org.in.
The dashboard has various sections such as Office suite, CCRAS Institute Websites, CCRAS Internal applications, Web portal - Informatics & Point of Care applications, Web portal - Knowledge & Literature, Web portal – Schemes, Web portal – Others, Mobile applications, Project specific applications, Applications under testing, CCRAS Journals, Social media pages and Web portal - legacy version long with a search functionality.
The details of the accreditation of CCRAS Institutes under the National Accreditation Board for Hospitals and Healthcare Providers (NABH) and the National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL) are enclosed as Annexure I.
The details of the Research Methodology textbook developed under Ayurved Prabodhini series are given in Annexure -II.

Annexure - II
Description of the book of CCRAS entitled ‘A Textbook of Research Methodology’
Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS) is the apex body of Ministry of Ayush engaged in the formulation, coordination, development, and promotion of research on scientific lines in the Ayurveda. This year, it has come up with a comprehensive text book under its ‘Ayurved Prabodhini Granthamala series’ on Research methodology especially in line with Outcome-based dynamic curriculum for the postgraduate scholars pursuing MD/ MS Ayurveda implemented by the National Commission For Indian System of Medicine (NCISM).
The syllabus for Research methodology has been designed keeping in view the utmost need to inculcate deep understanding and application of Ayurvedic fundamentals among the postgraduate students. The syllabus has been meticulously planned to offer students with a comprehensive insight into literature search, framing research questions, stating hypotheses, research design, data analysis, ethical considerations, and scientific writing.
There are twenty-one chapters in this book, designed to address the requirements as per different units of the respective six modules. This book is the outcome of joint effort of 34 scientists and 16 faculty comprising senior professors, domain experts and Research professionals from both Ayush and modern scientific streams. Each chapter has undergone through three stages i.e. structured drafting, peer review and phased editorial refinement.
This is the first of its kind effort of CCRAS to have a publication in this subject so as to ignite the postgraduate minds and make them competent with the research knowhow and associated skills for building a better career in Research in future.
This information was given by Union Minister of State (I/C) for Ayush, Shri Prataprao Jadhav in Rajya Sabha today.

enrichment.summary: CCRAS (Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences), the apex Ayurveda research body under the Ministry of AYUSH, has undertaken multiple research capacity-building initiatives: the 'PRAYATNA' scheme to train PG/PhD Ayurveda scholars in scientific writing, a Digital Initiatives Dashboard consolidating CCRAS's web resources, accreditation of its institutes under NABH and NABL standards, and a new textbook on Research Methodology under the 'Ayurved Prabodhini' series. This information was presented by Union Minister of State (I/C) for AYUSH, Shri Prataprao Jadhav, in the Rajya Sabha.
enrichment.context:
Ayurveda research in India has historically faced criticism for weak methodological rigor and limited high-impact publications, which has hampered its global scientific credibility and integration with evidence-based medicine. CCRAS, established to conduct and coordinate scientific research in Ayurveda, has been pushing for standardization through quality certifications like NABH (for hospitals/clinical research facilities) and NABL (for testing and calibration laboratories), which are the same accreditation frameworks used across India's mainstream healthcare and laboratory sectors, signaling an effort to bring Ayurveda institutions up to comparable scientific and clinical standards. The PRAYATNA scheme and the new Research Methodology textbook, aligned with the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine's (NCISM) outcome-based curriculum for MD/MS Ayurveda scholars, reflect a broader push to professionalize Ayurveda education and research output, addressing gaps in scientific writing and methodological training among postgraduate scholars.

This fits into the larger AYUSH Ministry agenda of mainstreaming traditional medicine systems through evidence-based validation, capacity building, and digital transformation (e.g., the Digital Initiatives Dashboard for centralized access to research resources). Such measures are significant for India's soft power projection of Ayurveda internationally (e.g., WHO Global Traditional Medicine Centre in Jamnagar) and for improving the credibility of traditional medicine research amid global scrutiny.

prelims_questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS):
1. It functions under the Ministry of AYUSH.
2. 'PRAYATNA' is a CCRAS scheme aimed at improving scientific writing skills among Ayurveda PG/PhD scholars.
3. NABL accreditation given to CCRAS institutes pertains only to hospital services and not to laboratories.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: CCRAS operates under the Ministry of AYUSH (statement 1 correct) and PRAYATNA is indeed its scheme to build scientific writing skills among scholars (statement 2 correct). However, NABL accreditation pertains to testing and calibration laboratories, not hospital services (that is NABH's role), making statement 3 incorrect.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Ayurved Prabodhini Granthamala' series, under which CCRAS released a textbook on Research Methodology, is aligned with the curriculum implemented by which of the following bodies?
options: National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM)
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states the textbook syllabus is designed in line with the outcome-based dynamic curriculum for PG scholars (MD/MS Ayurveda) implemented by the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM), which replaced the earlier Central Council of Indian Medicine (CCIM).

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of quality accreditation frameworks like NABH and NABL in strengthening the credibility and scientific rigor of traditional medicine research institutions in India, with reference to CCRAS.

Examine the challenges facing Ayurveda research in India and evaluate how capacity-building initiatives such as CCRAS's PRAYATNA scheme and standardized research methodology training can help mainstream Ayurveda within the global scientific community.
